about.lead: Three years of shipping. Production apps across Flutter, Next.js, and the messy edges in between — where QA automation actually matters.
about.p1: I'm a Full-Stack Developer and Systems Engineer from Honduras. My work spans cross-platform mobile (Flutter), modern web (Next.js 16, React, TypeScript), and the automation layer underneath — Cypress and Playwright test suites that keep releases honest.
about.p2: I graduated from José Cecilio del Valle University and hold professional certifications in Full-Stack Engineering and Computer Science. Lately I've been pairing that foundation with AI-augmented workflows: Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini as force multipliers, not replacements.

prizio.tagline: Price comparison for Honduran supermarkets — the first Flutter app in the country built for daily shopping.
prizio.description: Cross-platform price comparison app. Scan barcodes, compare prices across chains, set alerts, and build smart shopping lists.
body: Three national supermarket chains dominate Honduran retail. None of them publish standardized pricing. A single item — a 500g box of pasta, say — can vary by 30% between stores on any given day, and shoppers have no practical way to know in advance.

Prizio was built to close that information gap. Scan a barcode in-store, or search from home. See every price on the same screen, updated by a community of shoppers and merchant partners. Set alerts. Build a smart shopping list that routes you to the cheapest basket across your preferred chains.
Shipped on both iOS and Android with Firebase-backed sync, custom Sentry crash reporting, and a Cypress-inspired Flutter integration test suite covering the top 30 user journeys.

folium.tagline: Academic services platform with SEO-first content — 60 articles and a 26-service catalog at launch.
folium.short: Academic services platform with SEO-first content.
folium.description: Academic services platform with 60+ SEO-optimized blog articles, 26-service catalog, and MDX-powered content system.
body: Folium Labs provides thesis, research, and editorial services for university students across Latin America. The old funnel was a WhatsApp thread and a Linktree — no SEO footprint, no service transparency, no way for prospective clients to self-qualify.

I rebuilt the business on Next.js 16 with MDX-powered content, a typed service catalog, and Resend-backed contact flows. Sixty articles on thesis writing, APA, and research methodology were published at launch — each indexed, schema-annotated, and editorially reviewed.

Everything behind the scenes is typed end-to-end. Pricing, service catalog, and blog posts all live as static content that compiles at build time — no CMS, no runtime database queries, and deploy is a git push.

printshop.tagline: E-commerce with admin dashboard and invoicing — custom-built for a Honduran print shop.
printshop.short: E-commerce with admin dashboard and invoicing.
printshop.description: E-commerce platform with admin dashboard, React-PDF invoicing, Zustand-powered state, and end-to-end inventory management.
body: PrintShop 504 is a Honduran print-and-sign shop with a growing roster of walk-in and B2B customers. Before the rebuild, orders were tracked on paper slips, invoices handwritten, and inventory reconciled monthly (and unreliably). Missed reorders were routine.

I designed and built a custom e-commerce platform with an admin dashboard, a React-PDF invoicing system, Zustand-powered state, and Supabase at the backend handling auth, orders, and a live inventory ledger. Customers place orders online; staff fulfill them from a single dashboard.
Built solo on Next.js with Supabase, React-PDF for invoices, and a Cypress suite guarding the checkout and admin flows.

arca.tagline: Five-language non-profit platform — blog, gallery, donations, and a full i18n stack.
arca.description: Non-profit website with blog, gallery, donation flow, and full localization across Spanish, English, French, Portuguese, and German.
body: El Arca Honduras is a non-profit serving children and families with disabilities. Their work reaches an international donor base, but the old site was Spanish-only and static — missing translations, no gallery, no way to route donations programmatically.

I rebuilt it on Next.js with a full five-language stack (Spanish, English, French, Portuguese, German), a dynamic blog, a photo gallery, and a donation flow routing through the right regional processor.
Every piece of copy lives in typed translation files; no string on the site ships without all five locales. Built with the same stack I use for commercial work — translated, tested, shipped.

spotify.tagline: Generate playlists by mood, export to Spotify — live OAuth + Web API integration.
spotify.short: Generate playlists by mood, export to Spotify.
spotify.description: Search songs, generate playlists by mood, and export directly to your Spotify account. OAuth flow + live API integration.
body: Spotify's own UI exposes acoustic features — energy, danceability, valence, tempo — but only through its Web API. They're invisible to the listener.

This app surfaces those features as sliders. Set a mood, generate a playlist that matches, preview it, then push the whole thing straight to your Spotify account via OAuth. No saved credentials, no middleman — just the Web API and your account.
Built to learn OAuth flows properly. Every call is rate-limited, every error handled, every action undoable.

pharmacy.tagline: Internal pharmacy operations system — running quietly, unchanged, three years on.
pharmacy.description: Internal pharmacy operations system — inventory, billing, user roles, auth, and email-based password recovery.
body: Hedman Garcia Pharmacy is a family-run operation with thousands of SKUs and several staff handling sales across two shifts. Before the rebuild, billing was on a legacy cash-register system, inventory was eyeballed, and cross-staff reconciliation required end-of-day spreadsheet work.

I built a custom internal platform end-to-end: role-based auth with email recovery (SendGrid), unified billing, live stock adjustments on every sale, and staff-level reporting. Built on PHP and MySQL — deliberately boring server-side tech that family staff could trust and operate on modest hardware.
My first production system. Still running — quietly, unchanged, three years on.
